definition: An object with a north pole and a south pole that attracts magnetic materials and repels the like pole of another magnet.
One of the two ends of a magnet, north (N) or south (S), where its magnetic effect is strongest; like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
Magnetism produced in a magnetic material, such as iron, when it is placed near a magnet or in a magnetic field; the end nearest a magnet's pole becomes the opposite pole.
A magnet, usually made of steel, that is harder to magnetise but keeps its magnetism once magnetised.
A magnet, usually made of soft iron, that is easy to magnetise and loses its magnetism as soon as the magnetising field is removed, as in an electromagnet core.
A region in which a magnetic pole feels a force; its direction is the direction of the force a north pole would feel there.
A line drawn to show the direction of a magnetic field, running from the N pole to the S pole outside a magnet (Extended: the closer together the lines, the stronger the field).
A coil of wire, usually wound on a soft-iron core, that acts as a magnet only while a current flows in the coil.
